dev.action.aton.lab_login: LAB-2: log in as the duty shift
ui.aton.adv.balcony.1: The balcony round the lamp room: iron decking, a rail, wind off the sea.
ui.aton.adv.balcony.2: It is dark. The town on the shore can't be seen: not a window, not a street lamp. It isn't that it has been put out. It seems to have been taken in for the night, the way washing is taken in before rain.
ui.aton.adv.balcony.3: The lamp's light goes round: water, pier, roofs, water again. The town beneath it can be seen whole, to the last window. To the last, it would seem.
ui.aton.adv.balcony.s1: "He-ey!" No echo. For an echo, something has to be standing out there.
ui.aton.adv.cellar.1: The cellar. An oil tank the size of the wall, with a gauge on it. A pipe runs up from the tank, a valve on the pipe, and beside it a hand pump with a plate.
ui.aton.adv.cellar.2: The valve has no handwheel: a bare square stem sticks out.
ui.aton.adv.cellar.3: The valve is open. The "not a wheel" sits on it and, it must be admitted, looks like a wheel.
ui.aton.adv.cellar.4: Oil moves quietly in the pipe: up, to the lamp.
ui.aton.adv.cellar.c2: Fit the "not a wheel" on the stem and open
ui.aton.adv.cellar.c3: Turn the stem with your fingers
ui.aton.adv.cellar.s1: The needle stands at FULL. You tap: it drops to zero, lies there while you look, and goes back to FULL the moment you turn away. The day keeper was right: the gauge lies. But it lies politely.
ui.aton.adv.cellar.s2: The square hole settles onto the square stem as if they knew each other. Three turns to the left. Something in the pipe swallows.
ui.aton.adv.cellar.s3: The stem is cold, slippery and has no intention of turning. Something round with spokes obviously went on it. Something that somebody carried off and hung up out of the way.
ui.aton.adv.cellar.s4: You pump. The pump sighs, the pipe says nothing. The oil stays in the tank and isn't going anywhere while the valve is shut.
ui.aton.adv.dark_walk.1: A step. There is something under it to stand on. Another step. The crack of the door behind you has grown thin as a thread. You notice you have stopped feeling what your hands are like: long, short, whose.
ui.aton.adv.dark_walk.s1: One more step. The thread behind you breaks without a sound. You walk, and there is nobody to say how far you have gone, or whether it is you walking. The lamp did not burn that night. Nobody on the shore noticed: there was nobody to notice.
ui.aton.adv.dark_walk.s2: THE END. The watch was not handed over.
ui.aton.adv.dark_walk.s3: You turn and walk toward the thread of light. The steps appear under your feet reluctantly, but they appear. The tower smells of paraffin, and you are surprised at how good that is.
ui.aton.adv.dawn_out.1: You take hold of the wick screw and turn it down: slowly, counting the turns. Ten. Nine. Eight. With every turn something lets go: the gauge, the valve, the knock at the door, the forty steps. Five. There is less of you yourself, and it isn't frightening. Three. Two. One.
ui.aton.adv.dawn_out.2: Zero. The lamp goes out. And nothing changes: the light stays. It is simply no longer from the lamp. The pier is in place. The roofs are in place. The cat on the fence stretches: all of it, the whole cat, with no half turns about it.
ui.aton.adv.dawn_out.s1: The lamp room's glass is warm on both sides. The moths on the frame fold their wings: their shift is over too.
ui.aton.adv.dawn_out.s2: You go down, thirty-nine steps, and walk out of the door without signing. Outside it is morning. There are people standing on the shore, not many, ten or so, and all of them are looking one way: to where it is rising. The old woman in the headscarf is there too. She doesn't turn round, but she moves over so that you have somewhere to stand.
ui.aton.adv.dawn_out.s3: The jar in your hands is full to the top. You take off the lid. Nothing happens: what was in the jar and what is outside are one and the same. Your face is warm. You stand with the others and don't look back to check whether the tower is still there.
ui.aton.adv.dawn_out.s4: THE END. Watch handed over. There is nobody to take it, and no need.
ui.aton.adv.door.1: The door outside: oak, with a bolt. Notches on the jamb: somebody was marking either height or nights.
ui.aton.adv.door.2: It is quiet behind the door. Quiet not the way it is outdoors but the way it is inside a closed box.
ui.aton.adv.door.3: Knocking. Three times. A pause, exactly long enough to reach the door.
ui.aton.adv.door.4: The door is open. The visitor stands on the threshold and waits without stepping over it.
ui.aton.adv.door.s1: The bolt slides easily: it has been oiled more often than anything else at the post.
ui.aton.adv.drawer.1: In the drawer: a pencil stub, a matchbox, the tea tin and a rubber band that no longer holds anything.
ui.aton.adv.drawer.2: In the drawer: a matchbox, the tea tin and a rubber band that no longer holds anything.
ui.aton.adv.drawer.s1: The pencil is worn down at both ends. Somebody wrote a great deal. Or chewed a great deal.
ui.aton.adv.drawer.s2: One match rattles. You open it: burnt. It was put back carefully, the way you put back a thing that will still come in useful.
ui.aton.adv.drawer.s3: The tea is black, coarse, and smells of smoke and of dry grass from the sunny side. Scratched on the bottom of the tin: "for two".
ui.aton.adv.edge.1: You follow the beam with your eyes to its very edge. The edge is straight, like a tablecloth's. On this side: a street, a fence, a cat on the fence. On the other, not darkness. Darkness is when something is there and can't be seen. Out there it simply hasn't been made any further.
ui.aton.adv.edge.2: The beam moves on, and the street moves with it: houses stand up before the light and fold away behind it, without a sound. The cat on the fence exists for half a turn. It looks perfectly calm about it.
ui.aton.adv.edge.s1: The light comes back. Street, fence, cat. It sits in exactly the same place in the same way, as if it had never gone anywhere. From its point of view, that is probably so.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.1: The lamp room. In the middle the lamp, tall as a person, behind thick lenses; around it, glass from floor to ceiling and a door to the balcony.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.2: The lamp is out. Judging by the warm glass, it went out exactly when you set foot on the last step: it waited for a witness.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.3: The lamp burns evenly, without soot, and slowly turns its light over the water and the shore.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.4: One window sash is open. There's a draught; moths sit on the frame, waiting for something to fly at.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.c6: Look for something to light it with
ui.aton.adv.gallery.c7: Look for something to light it with
ui.aton.adv.gallery.s1: FULL. You tap: FULL. This gauge doesn't even pretend to think about it.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.s2: You close it and turn the catch. The draught is gone. The moths stay outside and look through the glass without resentment.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.s3: The wick comes up dry as last year's grass. There is nothing to light: no oil in the lamp, whatever the gauge shows. The oil is somewhere lower down.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.s4: You strike it on the sill. The match thinks for a second and lights. The air in the lamp room stands still, and the little flame stands straight in it as if drawn.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.s5: You strike it. The match lights, and the draught from the open sash takes the flame off it in one movement, like a hat. The moths on the frame seem no less disappointed than you.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.s6: That was the only one. There is just one fire left in the tower now: downstairs, under the kettle. If only it could be carried up here on something that burns.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.s7: Your pockets are empty. There used to be matches at the post, it seems: the box in the desk drawer. And something thin was sticking out of the log book.
ui.aton.adv.gallery.s8: Up here, nothing. There is fire downstairs, under the kettle. Paper burns. The only paper at the post is the log book.
ui.aton.adv.kettle.1: The stove burns with a small blue flame; it seems nobody ever puts it out. The kettle on it is cold: the flame is turned so low that it warms only itself.
ui.aton.adv.kettle.2: The stove burns. The kettle is hot and whistles softly through its spout, like someone with something to say.
ui.aton.adv.kettle.c1: Turn the flame up and make tea
ui.aton.adv.kettle.c3: Light the page and run upstairs
ui.aton.adv.kettle.s1: You turn the flame up and tip tea from the tin into the kettle: for two, as it says. A minute later the room smells of smoke and summer.
ui.aton.adv.kettle.s2: The tea is hot and slightly bitter. The glass warms your palms as if it had just been carried in out of the sun.
ui.aton.adv.kettle.s3: You twist the page into a spill and put its end into the blue flame. It catches at once. Forty steps at a run, your palm cupped; the little flame lies on its side but holds on. It seems curious itself how this will end.
ui.aton.adv.lastlamp.1: The lamp room at dawn. Beyond the glass the sky over the sea is growing light from one edge, and suddenly you see it: that light and the lamp's light are the same colour. Not a similar one. The same.
ui.aton.adv.lastlamp.2: Ships this watch: none. There never were any ships. The lamp isn't for them. It is for the shore: so that all night the houses have somewhere to stand and someone is there to drink tea. It keeps the place until morning, the way you keep a place in a queue for someone who is just coming.
ui.aton.adv.lastlamp.3: And you remember how the moth-eaten line ended. "In the morning the main thing, don't forget: put it out yourself."
ui.aton.adv.lastlamp.c2: Leave it burning and go down
ui.aton.adv.lastlamp.s1: Your hand won't rise to it. All that trouble with it through the night, and now put it out? You go down. The lamp hums at your back evenly and, it seems, with understanding.
ui.aton.adv.lens.1: Through the little dark glass on a chain you can look in behind the lenses. To be honest there is hardly any flame in there: a blue tongue the size of a fingernail. The light doesn't come from it. It seems to pass through the little flame from somewhere that has plenty.
ui.aton.adv.lens.s1: Your face is warm, as at noon by a wall. When you look away a round spot hangs before your eyes and drifts unhurriedly after your gaze: onto the wall, the floor, your hands.
ui.aton.adv.log.1: The log book. Thick, bound in oilcloth, the corners nibbled. Something thin sticks out between the pages: a bookmark.
ui.aton.adv.log.2: The log book. Thick, bound in oilcloth, the corners nibbled.
ui.aton.adv.log.3: At the spine, the fringe of a torn-out page sticks up.
ui.aton.adv.log.s1: Nothing to write with. A finger leaves on the page only what was on the finger anyway.
ui.aton.adv.log.s2: The pencil is already over the page, but you don't know how it's done here. Better look first at what they wrote before you.
ui.aton.adv.log.s3: "Took the watch. The lamp is being difficult." An entry like any other. Cover it with your palm, uncover the one beside it, and there is no telling them apart.
ui.aton.adv.log.s4: You tear out the last one, the blank one. The book sighs at the spine. The page is dry and old: it will burn well.
ui.aton.adv.log_mark.1: The book falls open by itself. The bookmark is a match: whole, with its head on. Moths have eaten the page under it, and eaten with discrimination: only the ends of the lines are left.
ui.aton.adv.log_mark.2: "…not for them. …as far as the edge, and beyond it no… …in the morning the main thing, don't forget to—" After that, a neatly shaped hole.
ui.aton.adv.log_mark.s1: There is one match. You feel it at once, the way you feel the last lump of sugar.
ui.aton.adv.log_old.1: The entries go night after night, and every night is the same one: "Took the watch. The lamp was difficult. Fixed it. Someone knocked. Opened. Handed over." Only the initials change: A., B., C., D.
ui.aton.adv.log_old.2: The initials differ. The hand is one: everywhere the letter "t" ends in the same curl, like a fish hook.
ui.aton.adv.log_old.s1: "The visitor asked for light in a jar. Didn't give any. Gave her tea." A page on: "The visitor asked for light. Didn't give any. Gave her tea." And a page after that. The jar, by all accounts, is the same one.
ui.aton.adv.log_old.s2: In the margin, in pencil: "Ships this watch: 0." And so on every page, in a column, as if somebody expected the figure to change one day.
ui.aton.adv.log_write.1: You write under yesterday's entry: "Took the watch. The lamp is being difficult." The pencil goes easily, as if along a worn track.
ui.aton.adv.log_write.2: Then you look at your letter "t". It ends in a curl like a fish hook. You look at the "t" one line up. Then one more up. There is no need to leaf back.
ui.aton.adv.log_write.s1: You try writing the "t" differently, on purpose. It comes out different. You lift the pencil: the curl is there. The hand added it by itself, out of politeness.
ui.aton.adv.predawn.1: The hour before dawn. The window turns grey. The lamp's light on the ceiling has grown paler: not because the lamp is weakening, but because it has a rival now.
ui.aton.adv.predawn.2: The log book lies open at tonight. All that's left is to sign.
ui.aton.adv.predawn.3: You have the feeling there was something you didn't see through or hear out tonight. But you can't ask the night to repeat itself.
ui.aton.adv.predawn.4: The jar on the desk glows from its bottom. The lamp hums upstairs. And for the first time tonight you don't feel like simply signing.
ui.aton.adv.predawn.c2: Go up to the lamp with the jar
ui.aton.adv.pump.1: The plate on the pump: "Ten strokes. Count aloud. From ten." Why from ten, it doesn't say. You take hold of the lever.
ui.aton.adv.pump.2: "Ten." The lever goes stiffly. "Nine. Eight." Easier. "Seven. Six." Easier still; with every stroke something seems to lessen in your head too. "Five…" And you can't remember what comes after five.
ui.aton.adv.pump.c2: Carry on from five, by guess
ui.aton.adv.pump.s1: The second time you get to zero. At zero the lever drops away like a step that isn't there, and oil starts moving in the pipe. What you were shedding along with the numbers, you no longer remember. Nothing important, probably.
ui.aton.adv.pump.s2: "Four?.." The lever agrees. "Three. Two. One." At zero it drops away like a step that isn't there, and oil starts moving in the pipe. Numbers, it turns out, remember themselves.
ui.aton.adv.radio.1: The radio: a dial, one knob, a handset on a coiled cord. One wavelength is marked on the dial in pencil and labelled "shore".
ui.aton.adv.radio.s1: "Shore, this is Lantern. Over." A second of hiss. Then from the speaker: "Shore, this is Lantern. Over." The voice is yours. The tone is yours. Even the breath before "over" is yours.
ui.aton.adv.radio.s2: The same on every wavelength: the sea. On one of them, it seems, a kettle; but that one is yours, behind your back.
ui.aton.adv.radio.s3: It hisses. Until the lamp burns properly, the radio apparently has nothing to talk about.
ui.aton.adv.radio.s4: "Shore, what's the time?" This time the answer comes before you finish: "The same as yours." And, after a thought: "There's only the one here."
ui.aton.adv.radio_listen.1: You hold the handset and keep quiet. You draw breath to say "Shore, this is Lantern". From the speaker, in your voice: "Shore, this is Lantern." You haven't said it yet. It already has.
ui.aton.adv.radio_listen.2: Then the voice begins to count, calmly, the way one counts before sleep: "Ten. Nine. Eight. Seven. Six. Five…" At five there is interference, as if someone had put a palm over the microphone.
ui.aton.adv.radio_listen.s1: "Four. Three. Two. One." At zero nothing happens. Only the lamp upstairs hums a little more evenly, and you notice you haven't heard your own heart for a while; it turns out it is in no hurry.
ui.aton.adv.radio_listen.s2: You click the switch. The dial goes dark. "Five," the speaker finishes, already without power, quietly, for the sake of order.
ui.aton.adv.relight.1: You bring the flame to the wick. The lamp doesn't take it at once: first it seems to sniff at it. Then a light rises inside the lenses, far too big for so small a flame, and you turn away, because it can't be looked at.
ui.aton.adv.relight.2: The light goes out through the glass and lies down on the water. After it, as after a hand, the shore comes up: a pier, roofs, a window, another window. In one of them somebody is already putting a kettle on, as if they had been doing so all evening.
ui.aton.adv.shore_dark.1: You go out. There is a step under your foot: exactly one, the one you have stepped on. Nothing can be said in advance about the next.
ui.aton.adv.shore_dark.2: Neither sea nor shore can be heard. Behind you is the yellow crack of the door. Ahead it isn't even dark; ahead it isn't anything.
ui.aton.adv.shore_night.1: The shore under the beam. Stones, a pier; by the pier rails go down into the water and shine beneath it like two wet threads. Small footprints lead from the door toward the town.
ui.aton.adv.shore_night.s1: You put your hand in the water. The rail is warm, like a handrail the sun has lain on all day.
ui.aton.adv.shore_night.s2: The footprints go evenly, unhurried, and end in the middle of the road: where the edge of the beam is now. When the beam comes back, there is one footprint more.
ui.aton.adv.shore_night.s3: From outside the tower is smaller than from inside. Forty steps wouldn't fit in it. Thirty-nine, perhaps.
ui.aton.adv.signoff.1: You write: "The lamp was difficult. Fixed it. Someone knocked. Opened. Handed over." And you put your initial. The hand writes "D." before you have time to think what yours is.
ui.aton.adv.signoff.2: A page is missing at the end of the log book. You decide not to write about that.
ui.aton.adv.signoff.c1: Read the day keeper's note again
ui.aton.adv.signoff.s1: "The lamp is being difficult. Don't trust the gauge. Tea is in the tin. If someone knocks, open. D." Every "t" ends in a curl like a fish hook. You put the note back in the same place. It will come in useful yet.
ui.aton.adv.signoff.s2: The bunk behind the stove is narrow and remembers the shape of your back. You fall asleep on the count of seven.
ui.aton.adv.signoff.s3: Evening. You take over the watch at the Lantern post. You don't catch the day keeper. On the desk is a note in a familiar hand: "The lamp is being difficult…"
ui.aton.adv.signoff.s4: THE END. Watch handed over. Watch taken.
ui.aton.adv.sleep.1: You lay your head on the log book. The oilcloth is cool. No light at all comes from above, and that makes the room very peaceful: suspiciously peaceful, like a house everyone has left.
ui.aton.adv.sleep.s1: You close your eyes and count yourself to sleep: ten, nine, eight… You don't get to zero. The lamp did not burn that night. In the morning there was nobody to check whether morning had come.
ui.aton.adv.sleep.s2: THE END. The watch was not handed over.
ui.aton.adv.sleep.s3: No. The lamp first. Your cheek has had time to learn the pattern of the oilcloth.
ui.aton.adv.stairs.1: A winding stair. Forty steps, if you believe the number cut into the bottom one. Halfway up, a narrow window.
ui.aton.adv.stairs.s1: Going up it comes to forty. Going down, thirty-nine. You try again: forty and thirty-nine. One step, apparently, exists in one direction only.
ui.aton.adv.start.1: NIGHT WATCH. A game for one keeper and one lamp. Written on night shifts and tested on them too.
ui.aton.adv.start.2: Evening. You take over the watch at the Lantern post: a stone tower on the shore with one great lamp at the top. The job is simple: it must burn until morning. You don't catch the day keeper. Nobody ever does.
ui.aton.adv.start.3: A note on the desk: "The lamp is being difficult. Don't trust the gauge. Tea is in the tin. If someone knocks, open. D."
ui.aton.adv.tank.1: You throw back the hatch on the tank. Oil to the brim: black, smooth, still. The lamp was never short of oil. It was short of someone to open the valve.
ui.aton.adv.tank.2: Your face is reflected in the oil. It is calmer than you expected.
ui.aton.adv.tank.s1: The reflection waves back: on time, not a second late. After the radio this is almost a little hurtful.
ui.aton.adv.tea.1: She sits on the edge of the chair and puts the jar on the desk, under the light. She drinks her tea from the saucer in small sips, and each time the beam crosses the ceiling she raises her eyes and waits for it to pass.
ui.aton.adv.tea.2: "You think you're guarding it," she says. "Nobody guards a lamp. You warm yourself beside it. All of us. You too." Then, her tea finished: "And what do you do in the morning?"
ui.aton.adv.tea.c1: "Hand over the watch and go to bed"
ui.aton.adv.tea.s1: "Every time," she agrees. "Every time you hand over and go to bed. Have you ever once seen who you hand over to?"
ui.aton.adv.tea.s2: She gets up, straightens her scarf and leaves without a goodbye, the way people leave till tomorrow. The jar stays on the desk. In it, at the very bottom, is a little light: as much as ran in over tea.
ui.aton.adv.tea.s3: "Nor do I," she says with relief. "Not one morning do I remember. So there must be something good there: the bad would have stuck."
ui.aton.adv.tea.s4: She gets up, straightens her scarf and leaves without a goodbye, the way people leave till tomorrow. The jar stays on the desk. In it, at the very bottom, is a little light: as much as ran in over tea.
ui.aton.adv.title: NIGHT WATCH
ui.aton.adv.train.1: Not a long wait. First a shiver runs over the water, as over tea in a glass on a carriage table. Then a train comes out from behind the cape: two carriages, round headlamps. It runs across the sea. The rails lie just under the water, and the wheels cut it into two thin whiskers.
ui.aton.adv.train.2: A warm light burns in the carriages. In one window there is a passenger: one for the whole train. He is looking at the lamp. As he passes, he raises a hand.
ui.aton.adv.train.s1: You wave. The passenger nods, the way one nods to an acquaintance one rides the same way with every day. The train passes beyond the edge of the light, in the plain sense, and doesn't rumble on out there but simply stops being.
ui.aton.adv.train.s2: You don't wave. The passenger keeps his hand raised right to the edge of the light: patiently, without reproach. According to the timetable glued to the rail, the return train runs "when possible".
ui.aton.adv.visitor.1: On the threshold is an old woman in a headscarf, small and dry. In her hands a glass jar with a lid, empty and very clean. "I'd like some light," she says. "In the jar. Just a little. To last till morning."
ui.aton.adv.visitor.s1: She nods without offence. "They all say that. On the first night." She doesn't put the jar away, though.
ui.aton.adv.visitor.s2: "From as far as it reaches." She points with her chin at the shore under the beam. "Beyond that there's none of me." She says it the way people say "I live past the bridge".
ui.aton.adv.visitor.s3: She looks past your shoulder. "Your kettle's cold. You put it on. I'll wait. I know how."
ui.aton.adv.watch.1: The watch room. A desk with the log book, a radio, a paraffin stove with a kettle. A nail in the wall. A door outside, stairs up, a hatch to the cellar.
ui.aton.adv.watch.2: On the nail hangs an iron thing with a tag: "NOT A WHEEL. Do not touch. D."
ui.aton.adv.watch.3: The light from the lamp upstairs comes unevenly. Or doesn't come at all: hard to tell from here.
ui.aton.adv.watch.4: The lamp's light crosses the ceiling evenly, once a turn.
ui.aton.adv.watch.5: Someone is knocking at the door. Three times, politely. Then three more, just as politely.
ui.aton.adv.watch.c5: Take the "not a wheel" off the nail
ui.aton.adv.watch.c9: Take a nap at the desk
ui.aton.adv.watch.s1: You take it down. Heavy, round, with spokes and a square hole in the middle. The tag is right about one thing: on its own it rolls nowhere.
ui.aton.adv.watch.s2: You sit. The light crosses the ceiling: a turn, another turn. Around the two hundredth you stop counting, and some time after that the ceiling starts turning grey by itself.
ui.aton.adv.window.1: The window looks out on the sea. The glass is thick, greenish, with an air bubble in it that is older than you.
ui.aton.adv.window.2: Beyond the glass it is dark so evenly that you can't tell whether it's far away or right behind the frame.
ui.aton.adv.window.3: Once a turn the beam crosses the water, and for a second the water under it becomes water: with ripples, with foam, with a gull that sleeps and rocks.
ui.aton.adv.window.c1: Wipe the glass with your sleeve
ui.aton.adv.window.s1: The glass gets cleaner. What is behind it doesn't: it was clean already.
ui.aton.advui.broken: The game tape cannot be read.
ui.aton.advui.hint: Pick a line with the mouse.
ui.aton.advui.intro: NIGHT WATCH. A game by the staff of Laboratory No. 2.
ui.aton.lab.mail.canteen.body:
Colleagues,

1. Eleven glasses have left the canteen this month. Glasses do not walk. Bring them back and no questions will be asked.

2. The kettle on the second floor boils water, not samples. Whoever did it knows who they are.

3. Close the small window in the machine hall at night: gulls. One has already sat on the plotter and watched it draw. It did the plotter no good.

4. Cabbage pie on Thursdays. Anyone who comes after one o'clock eats the timetable.

M. Kerimova, housekeeping
ui.aton.lab.mail.canteen.subject: Canteen: glasses and the kettle
ui.aton.lab.mail.census.body:
For your information.

The census set for this week has been postponed for the fourth time. The town office said what it said before: the new date will be announced to those who are found.

I submitted the laboratory's lists in advance. They came back marked "confirm the number". I confirmed it: there are as many of us as there were. The office replied that this was exactly what worried them.

Until the new date I ask everyone to be at their desks, or at least where you are usually seen.

Brandt
ui.aton.lab.mail.census.subject: Staff census postponed
ui.aton.lab.mail.chess.body:
For newcomers and guests.

The chess program has three strengths. The first hangs its pieces and does not mind. The second plays like a person after lunch. The third thinks longer and says nothing.

Nobody in the laboratory has beaten the third so far. Halvorsen has one draw, but it is disputed: the lights flickered that night and the program, in his words, "lost its train of thought". The program does not confirm this.

The list of wins hangs by the machine hall door. It is empty, but it hangs straight.

N. Oyamada
ui.aton.lab.mail.chess.subject: Chess: three strengths
ui.aton.lab.mail.count1.body:
Nobu,

remember I told you about the count? From ten down to nought, and at each number you let one thing go: small things first, then bigger. I was shown it in town, I won't say by whom, you would not believe me anyway.

Tonight I will try it on myself. The shift is quiet, the telescope is shut, clouds. I will sit at the terminal and at each number write down what I let go. Otherwise by morning I could not prove it even to myself.

I will leave the notes in my directory, a file called "count". If I am my usual self in the morning, we will laugh. If I am calmer than usual, we will laugh too, only more quietly.

I have switched the kettle off. In case you were going to ask.

T.
ui.aton.lab.mail.count1.subject: The count
ui.aton.lab.mail.count2.body:
Forwarding it as it is. In the morning the terminal was on, the chair pushed back, and Toomas was not there. I have changed nothing.

"10. The report, the plotter, the telescope queue. Let go. Turned out to be easy.

9. What they think of me in the canteen. Let go.

8. Whom I never answered and who never answered me.

7. That we will never understand one another. No one, anyone. This is harder. Sat a while. Let go.

6. My name. Strange: nothing changed without it.

5. The hands write by themselves. I watch them as if from a window. Not frightening.

4. Very quiet. I can hear how far it is. The sea seems to be count"

Nothing after that. The last line has no full stop; the file was closed in the normal way.

If anyone has seen Ilves since the night of the 22nd, tell me. Not the directorate. Me.

Oyamada
ui.aton.lab.mail.count2.subject: The file "count" (Ilves's directory)
ui.aton.lab.mail.count3.body:
Colleagues.

At Oyamada's request I checked the account of T. Ilves.

There is no account. Not "locked", not "empty". It is not there, and the log has no line saying it was deleted. By the log, no such user was ever set up here. The directory, though, is in place, and the file "count" lies in it. Whose directory it is now, the system finds hard to say.

I did not do this. I do not know how to delete a profile without a line in the log, and if I did I would not own up, but this is not that case.

Ilves's pass hangs on the board at the gatehouse. The watchman says he never handed it in; the pass "was just hanging there when I looked".

I will not restore the account from the archive until Ilves himself asks me to.

adm.
ui.aton.lab.mail.count3.subject: T. Ilves's profile
ui.aton.lab.mail.director.body:
Colleagues,

over the past month the laboratory's mail has discussed: the behaviour of passengers on a local train, the construction of the sky, counting from ten down to nought, and somebody's notebook from the canteen. Not one of these letters contains a unit of measurement.

I ask you to stop philosophy on the lab's mail. Observations go in the log, with a date and an error margin. Whatever has no error margin is to be discussed in the canteen, on Thursday, after one o'clock.

T. Ilves is listed as on leave. The application will turn up.

Separately: the plotter paper has run out. There will be more when the plotter explains what it did with the old lot.

I have still not received the quarterly summary for the mast.

Brandt
ui.aton.lab.mail.director.subject: On the contents of the lab's mail
ui.aton.lab.mail.flux1.body:
Colleagues,

I am putting together the quarter's solar flux from the mast, and I do not like it.

It is October. The sun is lower, the day is shorter, the flux is obliged to fall. It does not fall. It goes up and down, but not where the calendar says it should: on Tuesday it was higher than at noon in July, on Saturday again.

I have checked the sensor twice, the second time before a witness (Abebe held the ladder and an opinion). The dome is clean. The cable is whole.

For now I am writing in the log: "instrument sound, readings strange". If anyone has an explanation duller than mine, I would be grateful.

Halvorsen
ui.aton.lab.mail.flux1.subject: The mast: flux out of season
ui.aton.lab.mail.flux2.body:
I have found what it matches. I wish I had not.

Every day at noon Kerimova counts the people on the square from the canteen window: she needs to know how many pies to put in. Her notebook is tidier than our log.

I laid her notebook beside my chart. The curves lie one on the other. Many people on the square: the flux is higher. Rain, everyone at home: the flux drops lower than the clouds account for. On the day of the fair the pen ran into the edge of the paper.

I know that people come out onto the square when it is sunny. I allowed for that. Here it is the other way round: first they come out, and some ten minutes later it brightens.

I returned the notebook. I told Kerimova I was checking the clocks.

Halvorsen
ui.aton.lab.mail.flux2.subject: The mast: what it matches
ui.aton.lab.mail.flux3.body:
Ragnar,

the mast stands forty metres from the sea. There is salt on the dome, salt in the connectors and, I suppose, in your tea as well. When the square is crowded, every door and window of the grocery is open, and the glass throws a glint onto the mast. There are your ten minutes.

Wash the dome with fresh water. Wipe the connectors. Do not put the canteen notebook into the report as a data source: we will be asked why there are more pies on Thursdays and will have nothing to say.

I expect the quarterly summary by Monday, with the usual curve.

Brandt
ui.aton.lab.mail.flux3.subject: Re: The mast: what it matches
ui.aton.lab.mail.password.body:
Colleagues.

The duty shift's password has been found on a slip of paper again. Last time the slip lay under the keyboard. The time before, it was stuck to the monitor, and I took that for rock bottom. I was wrong.

Now the slip has been seen not even in the laboratory but in town: in the lobby of the Bridge House, on the upper terrace, in the letter pigeonholes. How it got there I do not wish to know.

If you happen to be up that way, please look into the pigeonholes and take it out. I have no time to climb up there: I am changing passwords.

I will not set a new password until the old slip comes back. This is not logic, it is upbringing.

adm.
ui.aton.lab.mail.password.subject: The duty shift's password. Again
ui.aton.lab.mail.sky1.body:
I am checking the catalogue before handing it in.

Field 14 and field 31 coincide. Not "resemble". Coincide: all one hundred and nine stars, down to the last faint one, with the same differences in brightness and the same close pair in the corner. The fields are over twenty degrees apart. They were taken on different nights, on different plates; one has my fingerprint on it, the other has not.

I checked whether I had filed one plate twice. No. I checked field 48. It coincides with field 14 as well.

If one goes further along that row, the sky, it seems, repeats like a pattern on wallpaper. I have not measured the step yet and, to be honest, I am in no hurry.

For now I am entering three separate numbers in the catalogue. Whoever is free on a clear night, come and look for yourselves.

Oyamada
ui.aton.lab.mail.sky1.subject: Catalogue: field 14 and field 31
ui.aton.lab.mail.sky2.body:
Nobu,

let me say at once: it was not us. The night shift does play jokes, but not ones this expensive. We could swap a plate; we could not forge your finger on it.

My money is on the plotter. It has already drawn the same sheet twice, and last month it drew a coastline that does not exist. If it drew your finding charts the same way, you pointed at one spot three times and never noticed.

And if it is not the plotter, I have a request. Do not measure the step. Let it be a sky whose step we do not know.

Thursday will be clear. I will come with a thermos.

L.
ui.aton.lab.mail.sky2.subject: Re: Catalogue: field 14 and field 31
ui.aton.lab.mail.sun.body:
My dears,

I have read it all. The mast, the sky, the train, Toomas. Halvorsen, you could simply have asked for my notebook.

I do not know which of you is right. None of you, I think, and there is no shame in that. For twenty years I have counted people from a window and never once been wrong about the pies, and I cannot explain why. I suppose some things add up because it suits them to.

It is clear today. I put the pie in and left. I am sitting on the square, on the third bench from the fountain, facing south. It is warm. Half the town is here already, and everyone is quiet, as in a queue for something good.

If you are reading this, you are still at the terminal. Get up. The log will wait; the error margin is not going anywhere.

Come. The seat beside me is free.

M. Kerimova
ui.aton.lab.mail.sun.subject: I am on the square
ui.aton.lab.mail.train1.body:
Not about work, but there is nobody else to write to.

After the night shift I take the evening train to the island, to air my head. I get off on the island; the train goes on, into the haze. I wait for the one back on the platform.

Three evenings running I counted. Going on, past the island: a woman with a string bag, two people in identical raincoats, a boy with a fishing rod and no line, an old man by the window. The same ones come back. In the same seats. The string bag is just as full. The old man looks out of the same window, only now it is on the other side.

None of them looks like a person who has been somewhere.

I asked the boy what is out there, beyond the haze. He said: "That's where they turn round." And pointed with the rod.

L. Abebe
ui.aton.lab.mail.train1.subject: The evening train
ui.aton.lab.mail.train2.body:
Lyova,

it is a local line. It always carries the same people. I know the woman with the string bag: on Thursdays she takes two pieces of pie from me and carries one away. So she feeds someone. So she lives somewhere.

As for people coming back just as they left, that happens to everyone. I went on holiday, came back, and nobody noticed.

But asking the boy and not the conductor, that was right. The conductor would have answered by the timetable.

Come on Thursday. I will keep you a piece, and you can see who she takes the second one to.

M.
ui.aton.lab.mail.train2.subject: Re: The evening train
ui.aton.lab.mail.welcome.body:
Hello.

This is a terminal of the Laboratory No. 2 network. You are logged in as a guest.

Open to guests: the weather station (readings from the mast, as they come), the game "Night Watch" (written by the staff outside working hours; the laboratory answers for none of it) and chess.

The duty shift's mail and the telescope queue open with the duty shift's password. The duty staff have it. If you are on duty and cannot remember the password, you are not the first.

Do not switch the terminal off. It takes offence.
ui.aton.lab.mail.welcome.subject: You are on the LAB-2 network
ui.aton.lab.session.open_guest: A guest has the weather station, the games and the common mail. The rest opens with the duty shift's password.
ui.aton.lab.session.open_staff: The shift's mail and the telescope queue are open.
ui.aton.lab.session.title: Laboratory No. 2
ui.aton.lab.session.user_guest: You are logged in as a guest.
ui.aton.lab.session.user_staff: You are logged in as the duty shift.
ui.aton.lab.session.wrong_hint: Wrong password. If you have forgotten it, look in the common mail: you are not the first.
ui.aton.scope.cloudy.2: The sky was closed. The automat waited until dawn and went to sleep.
ui.aton.scope.locked: The telescope queue is kept by the duty shift. It needs the shift password.
ui.aton.scope.result.double: The double star. Split cleanly: a gold one and a blue one. Their separation matches the catalogue to the last digit.
ui.aton.scope.result.evening_star: The evening star. A thin crescent, very bright. The automat cut the exposure three times.
ui.aton.scope.result.field14: Field No. 14. As many stars in the frame as last time. And the time before. Not one more, not one fewer.
ui.aton.scope.result.giant: The giant planet. The belts are visible, four moons counted. One of them carries a mark in the catalogue, with no explanation.
ui.aton.scope.result.moon: The Moon. The terminator is sharp, the crater shadows are long. Everything is in its place, and that is calming.
ui.aton.scope.result.rings: The ringed planet. The rings are wide open. The automat added: "beautiful", though that word is not in its dictionary.
ui.aton.scope.rules: Four slots a night. One slot may be yours. The observation runs by itself; the record appears in the journal if the sky was clear.
ui.aton.scope.title: Telescope queue
ui.aton.wx.footer: Readings are given as they are. The laboratory is not responsible for the weather.
